title: Repo market networks: dynamics under financial stress
summary: This ECB Working Paper uses transaction-level data from 2021 to mid-February 2025 to analyze how the euro-denominated repo market network responds to financial stress. The analysis reveals a core-periphery structure where a small group of highly active institutions conducts most trading. Connectivity between institutions, especially between banks, has intensified over time even during stress periods. Notably, the euro repo market functions as a shock absorber: borrowing costs decline as financial stress increases, with trading volumes and repo spreads remaining broadly stable at the sectoral level.
key_points: The euro repo market is the largest segment of the euro money market, accounting for 56% of daily transactions and 30% of outstanding amounts
The institutional repo network displays a core-periphery structure: a small core of highly active institutions does most trading, surrounded by a larger group of less active participants
Interconnections between institutions, especially bank-to-bank connections, have grown over time including during stress periods
At the sectoral level, trading volumes and repo spreads remain broadly stable under stress conditions
Financial stress is associated with lower spreads at the market level, indicating the repo market absorbs shocks through pricing adjustments

The analysis uses the Composite Indicator of Systemic Stress (CISS) to define financial stress and constructs institutional and sectoral networks from Securities Financing Transactions Data Store (SFTD) data
The euro repo market has grown 4.9% in total outstanding repos from June 2023 to June 2024
why_it_matters: This research is directly relevant to policymakers designing repo market regulations and financial stability frameworks. Understanding how the repo market network behaves under stress helps regulators assess systemic risks and interconnections between institutions that could amplify shocks. The finding that repo markets absorb stress through pricing adjustments rather than through volume disruptions suggests resilience in the secured funding market, which is critical for monetary policy transmission.
market_structure_context: The paper provides detailed analysis of euro repo market structure: the secured segment has grown to dominate, replacing much of the unsecured interbank market (which has contracted to one-tenth of its former size). The core-periphery network architecture means systemic risks can concentrate in a small number of highly connected institutions. Network metrics like density and strength are analyzed alongside repo variables (volumes, spreads, haircuts, maturities) across stress periods. The analysis from 2021 through February 2025 captures the post-pandemic normalization and the September 2022 LDI fund stress episode involving UK gilt repos with euro area counterparties.

4.9% growth in outstanding repos (June 2023 to June 2024)
